top_choice_rationale: Induced proximity has a mechanism that can be stated in physical terms: a small molecule shifts a binding equilibrium so that a ternary complex of target, ligand and E3 ligase forms, and ubiquitination follows from its lifetime and geometry. This is independently confirmed by kinetics, thermodynamics and structure, and it covers both PROTACs and molecular glues. The attributable core is compact and fits three laureates: the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type glues (Handa). Glues acting through cereblon are already in patients, so the principle is mature. P002 (Buchwald and Hartwig, C-N cross-coupling) is a mature and deserving second choice, but I rank it below P001 because it is less about a fundamental mechanism. A prize is better than no award.
